veranderings.voor: Hierdie kunselemente is reeds buite in die natuur self te sien.
veranderings.na: Jy kan hierdie kunselemente reeds buite in die natuur sien.
veranderings.rede: The passive 'is ... te sien' with 'buite' and 'self' stacked is wooden for Grade 4; an active sentence reads more naturally with the same meaning.
The pronoun refers to the plural veins (are/lyne), so 'hulle' makes the reference clearer than 'dit'.
Preposition: you see lines 'op' a leaf, matching 'op 'n foto'; 'aan' sounds unnatural with 'raaksien'.
'Regte' is the natural everyday word for a Grade 4 learner; 'werklike' is stiff.

veranderings.voor: Die ou blaar aan 'n tak kan diep groen wees en die nuwe een geel-groen.
veranderings.na: Aan 'n tak kan die ou blaar diep groen wees en die nuwe blaar geel-groen.
veranderings.rede: Putting 'aan 'n tak' first makes clear both leaves are on the branch, and 'die nuwe blaar' avoids the English-style prop word 'een'.
'Iets aanraak' is the natural Afrikaans for touching something; 'aan hulle raak' is awkward.
'Net 'n klein deel' is the idiomatic form; 'een' adds a counting sense the sentence does not need.

veranderings.blok: Hoe om te kyk en te beskryf
veranderings.voor: is daar 'n paar dinge om na te soek
veranderings.na: is daar 'n paar dinge waarna jy kan soek
veranderings.rede: 'Dinge om na te soek' copies English 'things to look for'; a relative clause with 'waarna' is the Afrikaans construction.

veranderings.blok: Hoe om te kyk en te beskryf
veranderings.rede: A lesson does not own names; 'die name uit hierdie les' says more naturally that the learner uses the terms taught here.

vlae.rede: The title writes one colour apart ('ligte groen') and the other as a compound ('donkergroen'); 'liggroen tot donkergroen' or 'ligte groen tot donker groen' would be consistent. The title cannot be changed by this step, so it is flagged for the writer or a person.
